decisions.reason: Bleaching tray blanks are thermoforming materials that sit squarely in the firm's core dental lab materials know-how, so the firm can interpret customer feedback and refine them with little effort, and they had their own page in both observed years.
A PETG thermoforming blank extends the firm's established blank and thermoforming portfolio, where its absorptive capacity is strongest, and it was consistently featured on its own page.

A UV-curing lacquer builds on the firm's chemistry and lab-material competence used for finishing earmolds and splints, so it fits existing knowledge, although its lower visibility (only mentioned) suggests a modest risk of portfolio pruning.

Custom hearing protection still draws on the firm's earmold impression and lacquer expertise, but the withdrawal of the broader custom earmold line suggests this downstream service area fits less well, raising the risk while retained visibility supports keeping it for now.
